title: Grid Enhancing Technologies (GETs): Trends and Implementation Guidelines
content: The modern power grid faces mounting challenges, including growing renewable energy integration, aging infrastructure, and increasing demand. Traditional methods for expanding transmission capacity, like building new lines, are costly, time-consuming, and subject to regulatory and public barriers. The U.S. Department of Energy’s Innovative Grid Deployment Liftoff report identifies pathways to accelerate deployment of Grid Enhancing Technologies (GETs). This paper focuses on key GETs such as Dynamic Line Ratings (DLRs), Advanced Power Flow Control (APFC), and Topology Optimization (TO). These technologies can boost capacity, improve power flow, and facilitate renewable integration in targeted applications. However, GETs are not universally applicable; in cases of rapid load growth, aging assets, or large physical distances between generation and demand centers, traditional infrastructure remains essential. This paper provides a technical analysis, highlighting optimal use cases and limitations, to guide informed decisions on deploying GETs in conjunction with conventional transmission solutions.
